=== water_feed (4 work orders) ===

-- incident key: home-place-temp:freeze_risk
[CRITICAL] Home Place: haul water now, tank at 9.1 gal with 4 F freeze, check heater and propane

home-place-temp reads 4 F, at or below the 10 F critical line, and home-place-water at the same site reads 9.1 gal in the same sweep. That pairing is the worst one on the ranch: a nearly empty tank that is also freezing, so what little water is there is likely unreachable to the 2 head on Home Place. The sensor series is not trustworthy as a trend: it swings from -6.7 F to 75 F inside an hour, so the temperature line itself may be faulty and belongs to infrastructure, but the tank reading stands on its own and gets treated as WATER-01 either way. home-place-propane reads 9.6% and home-place-diesel 10.8%, which matters because propane is what stands behind a tank heater here.

  1. Haul water to Home Place stock tank this shift: home-place-water reads 9.1 gal with 2 head on the 320-acre pasture. Do not stop to confirm the reading first.
  2. Before leaving the yard, check the well or windmill and, if solar-fed, the battery feeding home-place-water; a tank at 9.1 gal is usually supply, not consumption.
  3. At the site, check the tank heater and float at every water point in Home Place, not just the alarmed one, and chop ice if the heater is not holding.
  4. Check the propane behind the tank heater: home-place-propane reads 9.6%. Report the level to the office before you leave the site.
  5. Flag home-place-temp to infrastructure as suspect: readings swing -6.7 F to 75 F within the hour. Get a hand thermometer reading at the tank while you are there.

Not known from the sensors:
  - Whether Home Place has a working tank heater and what powers it (propane vs electric) is not in the packet.
  - Tank capacity and refill rate at home-place-water are not printed, so how far behind 9.1 gal is cannot be stated.
  - Whether Home Place is fed by well, windmill, or yard line, and whether that supply is solar-powered, is not in the packet.
  - No independent temperature source to confirm or refute the 4 F reading on home-place-temp.

ESCALATE: Freeze plus a near-empty tank at the same location is the WATER-03 worst pairing worked as WATER-01, this incident is on its second tick, and the temperature sensor is physically implausible, so the GM needs to know Home Place water is both critical and unmonitored.

Rules: WATER-01, WATER-03, WATER-05

-- incident key: weather-station-temp:heat_stress
[CRITICAL] Weather Station temp reads 102.4 F: run today's water route on every tank, and flag this station as untrustworthy

weather-station-temp reads 102.4 F, above the 100 F critical line, which under WATER-04 means water demand roughly doubles this afternoon. The sibling readings from the same sweep do not support a heat day: weather-station-snow reads 6.5 in of snow depth, weather-station-wind reads 50.6 mph, weather-station-humidity 49.8%, and the last 12 readings on this sensor swing from 34.3 F to 97.2 F in ten-minute steps. That pattern is not weather, it is a sensor that cannot be believed, which is infrastructure's repair under WATER-05. Severity stays critical as triaged, but the practical fact is that the ranch has no trustworthy air temperature right now, so nobody can tell whether the tanks are facing heat load or ice, and no pasture is mapped to Weather Station so there is no head count behind this reading itself.

  1. Treat the ranch as having no usable air temperature: run today's water route and put eyes on every stock tank and its well or windmill before dark, rather than trusting the station to tell you which tanks are under heat load

Not known from the sensors:
  - No true air temperature for the ranch, so it is unknown whether tanks face heat demand or freeze risk
  - No tank level readings in this packet, so which tanks are already at a warning level and should be pulled forward is unknown
  - No pasture or head count is mapped to Weather Station, so priority order for the route cannot be set from this packet
  - Whether weather-station-snow and weather-station-wind are trustworthy, or share the fault with the temp sensor

ESCALATE: The only air temperature sensor on the ranch is swinging 34 F to 102 F within ten minutes alongside 6.5 in snow depth and 50.6 mph wind, so heat and freeze decisions for every tank are currently blind and infrastructure needs to be tasked today.

Rules: WATER-04, WATER-05

-- incident key: alkali-flat-water:water_low
[WARNING] Alkali Flat, 111 head: tank 1 at 4.9 gal on today's route, check float and supply before dark

alkali-flat-water reads 4.9 gal, under the 6 gal warning line, with 111 head on the 2400-acre Alkali Flat pasture. Air temp on alkali-flat-temp is 62.7 F, so this is not heat driving demand; a tank drawing down on a cool day points at a leak or a failed float, and this incident has now been seen twice. The second tank on the same ground, alkali-flat-water-2, reads 25.4 gal, so the supply to the pasture is not obviously dead and the problem is likely at tank 1 itself. The last 12 readings on alkali-flat-water swing between 0 and 4.6 gal with three readings at or below 0.8 gal, which is either a float cycling badly or a tank that keeps emptying; treat it as a leak or bad float rather than consumption.

  1. Put Alkali Flat on today's water route, seen before dark: 111 head behind this tank.
  2. At the tank, check the float and look for a leak in the tank, valve, and line; the 62.7 F reading on alkali-flat-temp rules out heat as the cause.
  3. Check the well or windmill feeding Alkali Flat is running, and note that alkali-flat-battery reads 58% if the site is solar-fed.
  4. Compare against alkali-flat-water-2 at 25.4 gal on the ground; if that tank is holding, the fault is at tank 1, not the supply.
  5. Do not close on one good reading: confirm tank 1 holds level after the fix and report back.

Not known from the sensors:
  - Tank capacity for either Alkali Flat tank, so no fill or drawdown rate can be stated.
  - Whether the Alkali Flat water site is solar-fed or windmill-fed.
  - Whether the 111 head can reach alkali-flat-water-2 (25.4 gal) from where they are standing.

Rules: WATER-02

-- incident key: red-canyon-water-2:water_low
[WARNING] Red Canyon: 111 head, tank at 3.9 gal and air temp -17.4 F, check heaters and floats today

red-canyon-water-2 reads 3.9 gal against the 6 gal warning line, and the second tank on the same ground, red-canyon-water, reads 11.1 gal, so this is at that tank rather than at the supply. red-canyon-temp reads -17.4 F in the same sweep: that is a freeze, not consumption, and under WATER-03 a tank that is both low and freezing gets worked as WATER-01 regardless of the level band. The last 12 readings on red-canyon-water-2 swing from 0.2 to 4.9 gal in ten-minute steps with no trend, which is what a float sticking or ice on the sensor looks like, and this incident has now been seen twice since 16:24Z. red-canyon-fence reads 0 kV on barbed wire with the gate closed and red-canyon-battery at 64.8%, so power at the site is worth a look while the crew is there.

  1. Roll to Red Canyon this shift with water and ice tools: 111 head on 3100 acres, pasture status open, and red-canyon-water-2 reads 3.9 gal at -17.4 F

Not known from the sensors:
  - Whether Red Canyon's water sites have tank heaters, and what fuel or power is behind them
  - Whether red-canyon-water-2 is fed by the same well or windmill as red-canyon-water, and whether that supply is running
  - Why red-canyon-fence reads 0 kV: no energizer status or power-source detail on this page

ESCALATE: A low tank and a freeze reading at the same location is worked as critical under WATER-03, and red-canyon-water-2 has now appeared twice running, which points at supply, a failed float or an iced sensor rather than consumption.

Rules: WATER-03, WATER-01, WATER-02

=== herd_health (4 work orders) ===

-- incident key: cow-0905:deceased
[CRITICAL] Cow SW-1905 (cow-0905) recorded deceased, predator note: find the carcass today, no pasture recorded

Farm API records cow-0905, tag SW-1905, as deceased, last updated 2026-09-11T16:17:08.195Z. The high-severity injury observation at 2026-09-11T16:17:06.560Z reads: "Found down at first light, throat and hindquarter torn, tracks and scat consistent with coyote. Carcass is inside the fence line and the rest of the group is bunched and unsettled." An identical injury note stands at 2026-09-11T15:53:07.138Z, and between them a low general note at 2026-09-11T16:15:55.685Z reads "Chaos cohort restored to active after a demo. This animal is part of the chaos cohort and nothing recorded against it reflects a real event." That note contradicts the deceased status and the injury notes, and I cannot resolve it from this page, so the order stands as written for a predator loss. No pasture is recorded for this animal, so the crew cannot be pointed at ground yet; that is the first thing to establish.

  1. Ask the general manager or whoever wrote the 2026-09-11T16:17:06.560Z note where cow-0905 / SW-1905 was found; no pasture is recorded on the Farm API for her.
  2. Send a person to the carcass today: confirm the death, note the condition of the carcass and the ground and tracks around it, and record what they find as an observation against cow-0905.
  3. Have that person count the rest of the group against the roster and report whether any others are down, injured, or missing, since the note says the group is bunched and unsettled.
  4. Walk the fence line at the site on the same trip and report what they see to infrastructure; the note puts the carcass inside the fence line.
  5. Remove or dispose of the carcass on that trip so it does not draw the next predator.

Not known from the sensors:
  - No pasture is recorded for cow-0905, so the location of the carcass and of the rest of the group is not on this page.
  - Whether the 2026-09-11T16:15:55.685Z 'chaos cohort ... nothing recorded against it reflects a real event' note voids the deceased status and the injury notes.
  - How many head are standing in that group, and whether any other animal there changed state this sweep.
  - Fence, water, and weather conditions at the site: not mine to read, and none are on this page.

ESCALATE: HERD-01 requires escalation to the general manager on any deceased animal whose note points at a predator, and the GM also has to rule on the conflicting "chaos cohort / not a real event" note before the loss is booked.

-- incident key: cow-0512:care_overdue
[WARNING] Forest allotment hospital pen: pull patch and recheck pinkeye eye on cow-0512 (SW-1512), 24 days overdue

Care task task-cow-0512-0001, "Recheck pinkeye eye — remove patch", was due 2026-08-18T09:00:00.000Z and is still pending, 24 days overdue per triage. The only observation on this animal is 2026-08-08T11:00:00.000Z [medium] appearance: "Left eye cloudy and weeping — pinkeye. Pulled to hospital pen, patched." That means a patched eye has had no recorded look in the record since 8 August, and the Farm API last updated her status (active) 2026-08-10T14:00:00.000Z. This is not a shearing that slipped a week: it is a patch left on a treated eye with a month of no data, and the record cannot say whether the eye healed or worsened. She is in shelter hospital-pen on the forest-allotment (111 head on it); no other animal there read as anything but active this sweep.

  1. Go to the hospital pen on forest-allotment today and put hands on cow-0512, tag SW-1512.
  2. Remove the eye patch and look at the left eye: clarity, weeping, ulceration, whether the eye is still there and whether she is using it.
  3. Write what is found as an observation against cow-0512 with today's date, in the words of what was seen.
  4. Decide on site whether the vet is called; if the eye needs another look, open a new dated recheck task before leaving the pen.
  5. Close task-cow-0512-0001 as completed only after a person has been at the animal, with notes saying what the eye looked like.

Not known from the sensors:
  - Whether anyone looked at or treated this eye between 2026-08-08 and now: nothing is recorded, which is no data rather than a good outcome.
  - Whether the patch is still on the animal at all.
  - What treatment was given at the 2026-08-08 patching, and whether any is still due.

Rules: HERD-04, HERD-05

-- incident key: cow-0777:care_overdue
[WARNING] Red Canyon hospital pen: eyes on down cow SW-1777 today, recheck task 32 days overdue

Care task task-cow-0777-0001, "Recheck down cow — call vet if not up by AM", was due 2026-08-10T13:00:00.000Z and is still pending, 32 days overdue per triage. The only observation on this animal is 2026-08-09T07:30:00.000Z, [high] mobility: "Down in Red Canyon, hauled to hospital pen. Not rising, poor rumen fill." Task notes say "Hospital pen, banamine given." Farm API still lists cow-0777 as active, last updated 2026-08-10T14:00:00.000Z, pasture red-canyon, shelter hospital-pen. This is an overdue recheck on a down cow, not a slipped routine job: the record has no look at her since 09 Aug, and a month with no observation is a month with no data, not a month in which she was fine.

  1. Go to the hospital pen at Red Canyon today and lay eyes on cow-0777, tag SW-1777. First question is whether she is up.
  2. Call the vet from the pen if she is not up, per the task title "Recheck down cow — call vet if not up by AM".
  3. Record what is found as an observation against cow-0777, including whether she is up, rumen fill, and whether she is still in the hospital pen.
  4. Close task-cow-0777-0001 only once a person has been at the animal; if the record shows the recheck already happened, close it with the date it happened and who did it.
  5. If cow-0777 is not in the hospital pen, count the 111 head on red-canyon against the roster before assuming she moved back out.

Not known from the sensors:
  - Whether anybody rechecked cow-0777 after 2026-08-09 without writing an observation or updating the task.
  - Whether she is still physically in the hospital pen; the record says shelter hospital-pen but nothing since 2026-08-10T14:00:00.000Z confirms it.
  - Whether the vet was ever called after banamine was given.

Rules: HERD-04, HERD-05

-- incident key: sheep-0001:care_overdue
[WARNING] Lambing Pasture: shear the ewe band, task task-sheep-0001-0001 on EWE-101 is 6 days overdue

Care task task-sheep-0001-0001, "Shear ewe band", named against sheep-0001 (tag EWE-101) in lambing-pasture, was due 2026-09-05T09:00:00.000Z per the Care API and is still pending, 6 days overdue. This is a husbandry job that slipped a week, not a recheck on a sick animal: the Farm API records sheep-0001 as active, last updated 2026-08-10T14:00:00.000Z, and no other animal in lambing-pasture read as anything but active this sweep. No observation has ever been recorded for this animal on the Care API, so there is no data at all on her condition; that is a gap, not a sign she is fine. The pasture roster shows 78 head on 120 acres, so the shearing job likely covers the band standing with her, not one ewe.

  1. Send a person to lambing-pasture (78 head per the pasture roster) to shear the ewe band, starting with sheep-0001, tag EWE-101, as named on task-sheep-0001-0001.
  2. While handling the band, put eyes on each ewe and record an observation against any animal found off, since no observation has ever been recorded for sheep-0001.
  3. If the record is wrong and the band was already shorn, report that back so task-sheep-0001-0001 can be closed on purpose rather than left pending.
  4. Leave task-sheep-0001-0001 open until a person has been at the animals; do not close it from the office.

Not known from the sensors:
  - Whether the shearing was already done and simply not written back to task-sheep-0001-0001.
  - How many of the 78 head in lambing-pasture the "ewe band" task actually covers; the task names only sheep-0001.
  - Whether crew and shearing labor are available this week; the page carries no schedule.
  - Condition of sheep-0001 and the band: no observation has ever been recorded for this animal.

Rules: HERD-04, HERD-05

=== infrastructure (10 work orders) ===

-- incident key: antelope-ridge-fence:fence_down
[CRITICAL] Antelope Ridge fence dead at 1.4 kV, 111 head unfenced: get on the energizer this shift

antelope-ridge-fence reads 1.4 kV, below the 2 kV critical line, so the line is not holding. The last 12 readings on that sensor ran 5.0 to 8.4 kV, with 6.8 kV ten minutes before the drop, so this is a sudden fall rather than a slow bleed, which points at a hard short on the wire or a failed energizer rather than gradual vegetation load. antelope-ridge-battery is at 73.3%, so this is not the power source starving the box, and antelope-ridge-gate reads closed. Antelope Ridge is 2800 acres with 111 head, pasture status open, and antelope-ridge-temp reads 97.8 F, so the crew is working this in the heat. No wind reading is in this packet, so I cannot tie it to wind damage.

  1. Send a truck to the Antelope Ridge energizer this shift: check the energizer output, its ground rods, and the panel and battery feed (antelope-ridge-battery reads 73.3%, so start at the box, not the power)
  2. Ride the line from the energizer out looking for a hard short: downed wire, tumbleweed or limbs on the wire, cracked insulators, a gate handle hooked wrong
  3. Confirm with the general manager or whoever knows the ground whether any part of this run is a boundary or leased-allotment perimeter, and if so make the neighbour and road-side stretch the first section ridden
  4. Take a fence tester to the far end of the run and read voltage there before calling it fixed; do not close on a good reading at the energizer
  5. Report back on 111 head at Antelope Ridge, pasture status open, before leaving the pasture

Not known from the sensors:
  - Whether the Antelope Ridge run is a boundary/allotment perimeter or an interior cross-fence, and whether a county road adjoins it
  - No wind reading at Antelope Ridge in this packet, so wind damage as the cause cannot be confirmed or ruled out
  - Whether any crew member was working fence or gates on this line in the last hour

ESCALATE: INFRA-01 requires GM notification if this fence is a boundary or leased-allotment perimeter, and the packet does not say which stretch it is, so the GM makes that call now rather than after cattle are on someone else's ground.

Rules: INFRA-01

-- incident key: east-allotment-battery:power_low
[CRITICAL] East Allotment: battery at 9.7%, fence energizer at 0.4 kV - haul power and ride the boundary today

east-allotment-battery reads 9.7%, below the 15% critical line, after a series that ran 65.5% to 96.9% over the last two hours, so this is a fast collapse rather than a slow drain. In the same sweep east-allotment-fence reads 0.4 kV, which is an energizer with no push behind it, and the two are almost certainly the same failure: the panel/battery feeding that box is going down and taking the fence with it. This is a leased BLM perimeter, 4200 acres with 111 head on it, barbed-wire, pasture open, so loose cattle here is a neighbour and a lease problem. Both stock-tank sensors at this site (east-allotment-water 23.9 gal, east-allotment-water-2 11.6 gal) run off the same site power, so when the battery dies their silence stops meaning anything; water_feed owns what those levels mean.

  1. Send a truck to East Allotment this shift with a generator, charger, or spare battery; get the site back on power before it goes fully dark.
  2. At the site, check the charge controller and panel (dust, angle, wiring) before condemning the battery, then check the energizer, its ground rods, and its feed.
  3. Ride the East Allotment boundary line downwind and look for wire on the ground or a hard short; do not close this on a good reading at the box, read the far end of the run.
  4. Call the general manager: leased-allotment perimeter with 111 head behind an energizer at 0.4 kV, and the site's two tank sensors are about to go quiet.
  5. Flag that east-allotment-water and east-allotment-water-2 will stop reporting when the battery drops, so their last values should not be trusted as current.

Not known from the sensors:
  - Whether the East Allotment energizer runs off this same battery bank or has its own power source.
  - Whether the site has a pump on this battery, and what it feeds.
  - No wind reading at East Allotment in this sweep, so wind damage cannot be ruled in or out as the cause of the fence fault.
  - Whether there is a generator or spare battery already staged near East Allotment.

ESCALATE: Water site on a dead battery and a leased BLM perimeter fence at 0.4 kV with 111 head behind it, both of which INFRA-04 and INFRA-01 send to the general manager.

Rules: INFRA-04, INFRA-01

-- incident key: east-allotment-fence:fence_down
[CRITICAL] East Allotment: energizer dead at 0.4 kV with 111 head behind it, roll on it this shift

east-allotment-fence reads 0.4 kV against the 2 kV critical line, and the last 12 readings on that sensor sit between 0.1 and 0.9 kV, so this line has never been hot this afternoon: this is a sustained hard fault, not a blip. east-allotment-battery at the same site reads 9.7%, which is the most likely reason the energizer is not pushing, and that same battery is what keeps this site reporting at all. east-allotment-gate reads closed, so the containment failure is the wire itself, not an open gate. The East BLM Allotment is a leased federal perimeter with 111 head on 4200 acres and pasture status open, so cattle through this line are on somebody else's ground and a lease problem. Note also that the two stock-tank sensors here (east-allotment-water 23.9 gal, east-allotment-water-2 11.6 gal) run off the same failing battery and are about to go quiet; water_feed owns what those levels mean.

  1. Send a truck to the East Allotment energizer this shift with a charger/generator or spare battery: check the energizer, its ground rods, and the panel and charge controller feeding it, since east-allotment-battery is at 9.7%.
  2. Ride the east allotment line for a downed wire or hard short after working the box; a fence sitting at 0.1 to 0.9 kV all afternoon has a fault on it somewhere.
  3. Take a voltage reading at the far end of the run before calling this closed; a good number at the energizer does not close it.
  4. Call the general manager: this is a leased BLM allotment perimeter with 111 head behind it.
  5. Note for the crew that the two east-allotment tank sensors run on the same battery and will stop reporting when it goes; a silent tank sensor is not a full tank.

Not known from the sensors:
  - No wind reading at East Allotment in this sweep, so wind damage to the wire cannot be confirmed or ruled out as the cause of the short.
  - Not stated whether this energizer runs off east-allotment-battery or a separate supply, which decides whether the 9.7% battery is cause or coincidence.
  - No road or neighbour boundary detail for the east allotment perimeter, so the crew's judgment on where loose cattle go first is not in the packet.

ESCALATE: INFRA-01 requires GM notification when the dead fence is a leased-allotment perimeter, and 111 head are behind this one on federal ground.

Rules: INFRA-01, INFRA-04

-- incident key: met-tower-wind:high_wind
[CRITICAL] Wind Met Tower: 71 mph on met-tower-wind, expect fence faults downwind today

met-tower-wind reads 71 mph, above the 65 mph critical line. The last 12 readings on this sensor sat between 0.5 mph and 17.8 mph, with the newest at 17.8 mph, so this is a sharp gust event rather than a sustained blow that has been building, and it is the second time this incident has opened since 16:24:35Z. No other sensor sits at Wind Met Tower and no pasture is mapped to it, so there is nothing here to cross-check the reading against and no fence-voltage alarm in this packet yet. Wind at this speed is what puts wire on the ground: the thing to prepare for is the containment alarms that follow, not the tower.

  1. Radio the crew now: 71 mph on met-tower-wind, treat any fence-voltage alarm arriving this shift as wind damage on the same event, not a separate call.
  2. Ride the fence lines downwind of the met tower first, looking for downed wire, limbs and tumbleweed on the line, before checking energizers.
  3. Watch for drifted two-tracks and loose roofing at the home place and remote sites while moving between checks.
  4. Confirm the met-tower-wind reading against a second source (handheld or crew observation) on the next pass, since it is the only sensor at that site and the series it sits above tops out at 17.8 mph.

Not known from the sensors:
  - Wind direction at the met tower, which is what tells the crew which lines are downwind.
  - Forecast: whether this is a passing gust front or a sustained blow through the day.
  - No fence-voltage or gate readings in this packet, so no way to tell which lines are already affected.

Rules: INFRA-06

-- incident key: home-place-diesel:fuel_low
[WARNING] Home Place: order diesel and propane delivery now, diesel 10.8% and propane 9.6% with 4 F on the yard

home-place-diesel reads 10.8%, well under the 25% warning line, and its last 12 readings have run between 3.5% and 10.2%, so this tank has been sitting near the bottom of its range for two hours, not just dipped. The propane tank on the same yard, home-place-propane, reads 9.6% in this same sweep, so both reserves at the home place are low at once. home-place-temp reads 4 F with home-place-humidity at 61.9%, which is the freeze case INFRA-05 point 3 warns about: propane is what feeds tank heaters and cab heat exactly when a truck may not get in. This is a lead-time problem, so the delivery gets ordered on this shift even though the band is warning.

  1. Call the fuel supplier today and schedule both loads: diesel on home-place-diesel at 10.8% and propane on home-place-propane at 9.6%.
  2. Tell the supplier the yard is at 4 F per home-place-temp so propane is prioritized over diesel if only one load can move.
  3. Before the truck comes, eyeball both tank gauges at the home place against the sensor readings to confirm the levels are real and not a stuck float.
  4. Get the delivery date back to the office in writing so generators, feed trucks and the loader can be planned around it.

Not known from the sensors:
  - Tank capacities in gallons for home-place-diesel and home-place-propane, so no volume to order can be stated here.
  - Current burn rate on generators, feed trucks and the loader, so days of supply is not calculated per INFRA-05 point 4.
  - Forecast beyond the 4 F now on home-place-temp, which would say how hard the propane call is.
  - Whether a delivery is already on the schedule from the first sighting of this incident at 16:24Z.

Rules: INFRA-05

-- incident key: south-windbreak-temp:sensor_fault
[WARNING] South Windbreak: air temp probe reads -500 F, dead probe, run spares and swap it

south-windbreak-temp is reading -500 F, outside the physical band (-80 to 140 F), and it has held -500 F flat for all 12 readings in the series from 14:35 to 16:25 Z. That is a failed probe or a broken connector/cable, not weather; the number says nothing about conditions at the site. The other instruments at South Windbreak came back in this same sweep and look normal: south-windbreak-humidity at 36% and south-windbreak-gate closed, so the site still has power and uplink and this is one instrument, not a site outage. What went blind is air temperature at South Windbreak, which is a site rather than grazing ground, so no pasture is mapped to it.

  1. Load spare air temperature probe, connector, and cable and drive to South Windbreak.
  2. At the post, inspect the probe cable and connector for chew, corrosion, or a pulled pin, then swap the probe and confirm it reports a value inside -80 to 140 F.
  3. While on site, eyeball the windbreak and confirm the gate reads as south-windbreak-gate reported (closed).
  4. Treat South Windbreak air temperature as unmonitored on the board until the swapped probe reports in range.

Not known from the sensors:
  - No battery-charge or panel reading for South Windbreak in this packet, so power at the post is unconfirmed even though the other two sensors reported.
  - No record of when this probe was last serviced or whether a spare temperature probe is on hand in the shop.

Rules: SENSOR-03, SENSOR-05

-- incident key: windmill-pasture-battery:power_low
[WARNING] Windmill Pasture: battery at 28.7783%, check panel and controller; both tank sensors now unreliable

windmill-pasture-battery reads 28.7783%, below the 30% warning line, and this is the second tick on this incident since 16:24Z. The site is drawing down faster than the panel replaces it, and the two stock-tank sensors on the same ground are already showing it: windmill-pasture-water is degraded at 11.4 gal and windmill-pasture-water-2 is offline with no reading at all. That means this is a solar water site, so the silence from those probes is about to stop being informative: an unmonitored tank and a full tank look the same from here. windmill-pasture-fence is at 5.4 kV and the gate reads closed, so containment is holding for the 111 head on this 1900 acres for now. Note the recent series for this battery swings from 9.3% to 99% between ten-minute reads, which is not a physical discharge curve, so the charge controller or the sense line is a live suspect alongside the panel.

  1. Go to Windmill Pasture this shift: clear and inspect the panel (dust, angle, shading) and check the charge controller and battery terminals before condemning the battery.
  2. Take a charger or spare battery on the truck so the site can be brought back up on the same trip.
  3. While on site, eyeball the two tank-level probes: windmill-pasture-water reading 11.4 gal degraded and windmill-pasture-water-2 offline, and note whether they lose power with the battery or are separately faulted.
  4. Report to water_feed that both tank sensors at this site are unreliable so the tank is effectively unmonitored until power is restored; do not write the water call from here.
  5. Notify the general manager that this is a solar water site with a battery below the warning line.

Not known from the sensors:
  - What this battery actually powers at the site (pump, telemetry radio, or both) is not stated in the packet.
  - No wind or cloud-cover reading at Windmill Pasture in this sweep, so panel output cannot be judged against weather.
  - Whether windmill-pasture-water-2 went offline from loss of power or from its own fault is unknown until someone is on site.
  - Battery bank capacity and panel rating are not in the packet, so no charge or discharge rate can be quoted.

ESCALATE: INFRA-04 requires escalation to the general manager because this is a water site: a dead battery at a stock tank is a water emergency in electrical costume.

[WARNING] Windmill Pasture: both tank probes bad, battery at 28.8% - roll a truck with probe and battery spares

windmill-pasture-water reports degraded while still producing values; its authoritative current reading is 11.4 and the last 12 readings from this probe swing between 3.9 gal and 29.5 gal with no pattern, so its numbers are unreliable in both directions, high as easily as low. The second tank probe at this location, windmill-pasture-water-2, came back with no reading at all, status offline, so there is no sibling value to cross-check against and both instruments on this ground are out at once. windmill-pasture-battery reads 28.7783%, which is the most likely common cause and is checked before hardware. The fence energizer windmill-pasture-fence still reads 5.4 kV and the gate reads closed, so containment instrumentation is still answering; what has gone blind is water level at Windmill Pasture, 1900 acres with 111 head standing on it. Tank level itself and what it means for those cattle belong to water_feed, who is already being told.

  1. Roll to Windmill Pasture with tank-probe spares, connectors, and a replacement battery; this degraded probe goes ahead of any dark sensor of the same age in the queue
  2. At the site read windmill-pasture-battery on the panel first (last telemetry 28.7783%) and check panel, charge controller, and connections before touching the probes
  3. Swap or repair the windmill-pasture-water probe and its cable, then bring windmill-pasture-water-2 back up or replace the unit
  4. Put eyes on both tanks and the windmill while on site and report actual level to water_feed rather than through this order
  5. Confirm both probes are reporting real values before leaving; until then log Windmill Pasture water as unmonitored

Not known from the sensors:

  - Tank capacity and the true water level at either tank, since neither probe can be trusted

ESCALATE: Two tank sensors at Windmill Pasture are out in the same sweep, one degraded and windmill-pasture-water-2 dark, with windmill-pasture-battery at 28.7783%, which points at site power rather than two independent instrument failures.

report.headline: Home Place tank near dry at 4 F, three sites lost fence or power, and the ranch has no air temp it can trust
report.situation: Two sites carry the shift. Home Place has 9.1 gal in the tank at a reported 4 F with propane at 9.6% and diesel at 10.8%, so the water, the heater fuel and the delivery lead time are one problem in one yard, and the temp sensor there swings -6.7 F to 75 F so nobody knows what it is really doing. East Allotment is one failure seen twice: battery collapsed from 65-97% to 9.7% and the energizer on the leased BLM perimeter reads 0.4 kV with 111 head behind it, and the same battery is what keeps east-allotment-water at 23.9 gal and water-2 at 11.6 gal reporting, so those numbers go stale the moment it dies. Windmill Pasture is the same shape in miniature: battery at 28.8% with one tank probe degraded at 11.4 gal and the other dark, which means 111 head with an unmonitored tank, not a full one. Met tower at 71 mph against a series topping out at 17.8 mph is the likely reason Antelope Ridge fell from 6.8 kV to 1.4 kV in one step with a healthy 73.3% battery, though we have no wind reading at Antelope Ridge to prove it. Separately, the only air temperature on the ranch is unusable: weather station says 102.4 F alongside 6.5 in snow and 50.6 mph wind, South Windbreak reads a flat -500 F, and Home Place is implausible, so heat-versus-freeze calls at every tank are being made blind.
priorities: Haul water to Home Place now and take propane and a hand thermometer: 9.1 gal is the only reading here that can be acted on without confirmation, and a freezing near-empty tank is irreversible for the animals on it fastest. Only 2 head, but it is the yard and it is the shortest drive.

East Allotment next, with generator or spare battery and fence tester: restore site power first because the 9.7% battery is the cause and the 0.4 kV perimeter is the symptom. 111 head on leased federal ground with a fence that has not been hot all afternoon, and the two tank sensors go quiet with the battery.

Antelope Ridge energizer and line, same shift: 111 head, fence at 1.4 kV, battery fine at 73.3%, so start at the box then ride the line downwind of the 71 mph gust. Ride any boundary or road-side stretch first once the GM tells us which stretch it is.

Red Canyon on today's route with water and ice tools, and the same trip lays eyes on down cow SW-1777 in the hospital pen there: tank 2 at 3.9 gal at -17.4 F, sibling tank at 11.1 gal so the fault is at that tank, and red-canyon-fence reads 0 kV. One drive covers a freezing tank behind 111 head, a 32-day-overdue recheck on a cow that was not rising, and a fence with no push.

Windmill Pasture with battery, charger and tank-probe spares: check panel and charge controller before condemning anything, then get both probes reporting and report actual tank levels by eye. 111 head with water level unknown, which is why this rides ahead of Alkali Flat.

Then Alkali Flat tank 1 before dark (4.9 gal, 111 head, 62.7 F rules out heat, second tank holding at 25.4 gal so look for a leak or bad float), and on the water route also swing the forest allotment hospital pen to pull the patch on SW-1512, plus somebody to Coyote Draw gate, which was never worked, and the lambing pasture shearing when hands free up.
escalations: East Allotment is a leased BLM perimeter at 0.4 kV with 111 head behind it and the site battery at 9.7%: GM call now, before cattle are on federal or neighbour ground.
GM needs to say tonight whether the Antelope Ridge run is boundary/allotment perimeter or interior cross-fence; the crew cannot pick which section to ride first without it.
Home Place is critical and unmonitored at once: 9.1 gal, propane 9.6%, diesel 10.8%, and a temperature sensor that cannot be believed. Order both fuel loads today, propane first.

The ranch has no trustworthy air temperature anywhere: weather station 102.4 F with 6.5 in snow and 50.6 mph wind, South Windbreak flat at -500 F, Home Place swinging 80 degrees in an hour. Every heat or freeze decision is a guess until instruments are fixed. Also: GM must rule on the 'chaos cohort, nothing recorded reflects a real event' note against deceased cow SW-1905, and tell us where she was found, because no pasture is recorded and the predator loss cannot be booked or the carcass located without it.
